rules.title: Three-day Notice to Quit for disorderly, destructive or rule-violating conduct
rules.requirement: A landlord must give a three-day written Notice to Quit before evicting for causes described as disorderly, destructive or violative of written rules or lease provisions. No further notice is required before going to court when a tenant stays after failing to pay rent.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants being evicted for disorderly or destructive conduct or for violating written rules or lease provisions.
rules.quoted_span: A three-day written Notice to Quit is required for any of the causes described as disorderly, destructive or violative of written rules or lease provisions (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2(a)).

rules.title: Lease-expiration eviction in owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings
rules.requirement: A tenant in an owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling may be evicted if the tenant stays after the lease expires and the landlord has given written notice for delivery of possession. A three-month notice to quit is required for at will or year-to-year tenancies and a one-month notice for month-to-month tenancies.
rules.key_value: three-month notice (at will or year-to-year); one-month notice (month-to-month)
rules.coverage_text: Tenants residing in owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings.
rules.quoted_span: In addition to the causes listed above, a tenant residing in an owner- occupied two- or three-family dwelling may be evicted if the landlord can show that the tenant is staying after the expiration of the lease and the landlord has given the tenant a written notice for delivery of possession of the property. Under this cause of not renewing the lease, a three-month notice to quit must be given if an at will tenancy or year -to year tenancy exists. A one-month notice to quit is required for a month-to-month tenancy.

rules.title: Rooming and boarding house evictions
rules.requirement: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, unless otherwise ordered by the Bureau. The owner must also give at least three working days' notice to the County Welfare Board before starting an eviction action.
rules.key_value: at least three (3) working days' notice to the County Welfare Board
rules.coverage_text: Rooming and boarding houses: buildings with at least two living units occupied by unrelated persons without private kitchens and bathrooms, unless an exception in the Rooming and Boarding House Act applies.
rules.exemptions: Hotels with more than 85 percent temporary occupancy by people with homes elsewhere, school and college dormitories, buildings housing only college students and certain residences for the disabled are excepted from the rooming or boarding house definition; the good-cause requirement applies except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau.
rules.quoted_span: require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau (N.J.A.C. 5:27-3.3(c)).

rules.title: Owner-occupancy eviction: six-month occupancy requirement
rules.requirement: After a tenant vacates following notice that the landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit, the landlord must occupy the unit for at least six months. If the landlord instead lets another tenant occupy it or registers a condominium or cooperative conversion, the landlord is liable to the former tenant for three times the damages plus attorney fees and costs.
rules.key_value: at least six (6) months owner occupancy
rules.coverage_text: Units vacated after a notice that the landlord wishes to personally occupy the unit.
rules.penalty: Liability to the former tenant for three (3) times the damages suffered plus attorney fees and costs.
rules.quoted_span: If instead the landlord permits personal occupancy of the unit by another tenant or registration of conversion of the property to a condominium or cooperative, the landlord is liable to the former tenant for three (3) times the damages suffered plus attorney fees and costs

rules.title: Removal from residential use: five-year bar
rules.requirement: After a tenant vacates following notice that the landlord will permanently board up, demolish or retire the building from residential use, the landlord must not use the property for residential use for five years. Violations may bring liability of three times damages plus attorney fees and costs and a civil penalty up to $10,000.00 per violation.
rules.coverage_text: Units vacated after a notice that the landlord seeks to permanently board up or demolish the building or permanently retire it from residential use.
rules.penalty: Liability to the tenant for three (3) times the damages plus attorney fees and costs; civil penalty up to $10,000.00 for each violation; property may not be registered as a planned real estate development during the five-year period.
rules.quoted_span: When a tenant vacates a dwelling unit after having been given notice that the landlord seeks to permanently board up or demolish the building or to permanently retire it from residential use, the landlord must not use this property for residential use for a period of five (5) years.

rules.title: 90-day notice to quit after foreclosure purchase for owner occupancy
rules.requirement: Foreclosure alone is not grounds for eviction. A tenant may be evicted after foreclosure only with a 90-day notice to quit when the buyer wants to personally occupy the property as a primary residence, and a tenant whose lease runs beyond 90 days cannot be evicted until the lease expires and the notice has been given.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants in foreclosed properties purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy the property as a primary residence, including month-to-month tenants and two- and three-family owner-occupied units.
rules.citation: Chase Manhattan Bank v. Josephson, 135 N.J. 209 (1994)
rules.quoted_span: Before a tenant can be evicted due to foreclosure, the landlord must provide the tenant with a 90 -day notice to qui t when the foreclosed property has been purchased by a buyer who wants to personally occupy it as his or her primary residence.
rules.interaction_text: However, the federal law does not preempt any State or local law that provides longer time periods or other additional protections for tenants  in foreclosure proceedings .

rules.title: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act
rules.requirement: Eligible senior citizens and disabled tenants in buildings being converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership may be protected from eviction for 40 years if family income is not more than three times the average per person income in their county or $50,000.00, whichever is greater.
rules.key_value: 40 years protection; income not more than three (3) times county average per person income or $50,000.00, whichever is greater
rules.coverage_text: Tenants at least 62 years of age before the conversion recording date, permanently disabled tenants, or certain honorably discharged veterans disabled at 60% or higher from service, who have lived in a building being converted to a condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership at least one year prior to the conversion recording date.
rules.quoted_span: Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28).
